content.title: About
content.content: The frozen coffee drink is a ready‑to‑serve beverage made from cold coffee, sugar and dairy components, frozen to a soft‑serve ice‑cream consistency. It combines the aroma of freshly brewed coffee with a refreshing chill, perfect for hot days.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first frozen coffee drink appeared in Japan in the 1990s under the brand “Frappuccino”.
Stabilizers are often added to prevent ice crystal formation and keep a creamy texture.
It can be made at home using coffee syrup, milk and liquid nitrogen.
There are many flavor variations: vanilla, caramel, mint, chocolate, and spiced.

items.title: Source of caffeine
items.content: Caffeine boosts alertness and may improve concentration.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Coffee is rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: Sugar and dairy proteins provide a quick energy boost.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Caffeine stimulates dopamine production, contributing to a better mood.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: High caffeine intake can cause anxiety, insomnia, and rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High sugar levels may contribute to weight gain and increase diabetes risk.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Dairy ingredients can cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the frozen coffee drink in a glass with a straw; you can top it with whipped cream, dust with cocoa powder, or add a scoop of ice cream for extra richness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the freezer at –18 °C. Over time ice crystals may form; let the drink sit at room temperature for 2–3 minutes before serving to soften.

content.title: About
content.content: Poultry Gravy, Fat Free (1920) is a ready‑to‑use sauce made from lean chicken broth thickened with starch. It delivers a rich poultry flavor without any added fat, making it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Poultry gravy has long been a staple in European cuisine to enhance meat dishes.
The absence of fat gives this gravy a lower calorie count compared with traditional versions.
Starch thickening allows the sauce to set quickly without prolonged boiling.
It is frequently used in diet programs, including weight‑loss regimens.
The unopened product can be stored at room temperature; once opened, it stays fresh in the fridge for up to 7 days.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: No added fat makes the gravy compatible with heart‑healthy eating patterns.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Chicken broth provides protein that supports muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: The broth supplies vitamin B6, which aids protein metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: Sodium content helps maintain electrolyte balance when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: A lean composition is gentle on the stomach, suitable for those with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: The gravy can be salty; individuals monitoring salt intake should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: People allergic to poultry should avoid this product.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate
items.content: Some formulations may contain added MSG, which may not be suitable for everyone.

items.title: Shelf life after opening
items.content: Once opened, keep refrigerated and use within a week.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Use the fat‑free poultry gravy in stews, soups, casseroles, or as a sauce for vegetables and potatoes. Heat gently to a boil while stirring until it thickens.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened package in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep refrigerated at 0 °C–4 °C and consume within 7 days.

grilled-cheese-sandwich-cheddar-cheese-o.title: Grilled cheese sandwich, cheddar cheese, on white bread

content.title: About
content.content: A grilled cheese sandwich with cheddar is a hot sandwich made from slices of white bread with melted cheddar cheese inside. The sandwich is typically toasted on a skillet or grill until the bread is golden and crispy and the cheese becomes gooey.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The grilled cheese sandwich became popular in the United States in the early 20th century as a quick lunch for schoolchildren and workers.
Cheddar is one of the world’s most popular cheeses; its name comes from the English town of Cheddar where the cheese was first produced in the 12th century.
The classic recipe uses only two ingredients – bread and cheese – but butter is often added to the outside of the bread for extra crunch.
Variations may include tomato, ham, bacon, or spices, though the plain version remains the most common.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cheddar cheese is rich in calcium, which is essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: The cheese provides complete animal protein needed for tissue repair and growth.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of bread carbohydrates and cheese fats quickly replenishes energy.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: Warm, melty cheese and crunchy bread help promote a feeling of fullness.

items.title: High in fat and calories
items.content: The sandwich can be calorie‑dense and contain saturated fats, so it should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheddar contains lactose, which may cause discomfort for those who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: People allergic to dairy should avoid this sandwich.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheddar is salty; individuals monitoring sodium intake should take this into account.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich hot, cut in half. It can be enjoyed as a snack on its own or paired with soup, salad, or vegetable chips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Grilled cheese is best eaten immediately. If you need to store it, let it cool to room temperature, then place in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat until the cheese is fully melted before serving.

industrial-oil-as-ingredient-in-food.title: Industrial oil as ingredient in food

content.title: About
content.content: Industrial oil refers to plant or animal oils that are produced through large‑scale processing and used in the food industry as an ingredient, emulsifier, flavor carrier, or fat source. Common examples include refined rapeseed, sunflower, soybean, palm and other oils that have undergone cleaning and refining.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Industrial oils are often refined to a nearly neutral taste and odor, making them highly versatile in food applications.
A large share of the world’s vegetable oil production is destined for food manufacturing.
Refining removes free fatty acids, aromatic compounds and impurities, which extends product shelf life.
Some oils, such as palm oil, are frequently discussed due to their environmental impact.
Industrial oils can be fortified with vitamins (e.g., vitamin E) to enhance nutritional value.

items.title: Source of essential fatty acids
items.content: Many vegetable oils contain linoleic and alpha‑linolenic acids, which are essential for normal body functions.

items.title: Vitamin E enrichment
items.content: During refining, vitamin E is often retained or added, providing a strong antioxidant effect.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Fats are a concentrated source of calories, useful for individuals with higher energy needs.

items.title: Improves product texture
items.content: Oils help form emulsions, keep baked goods tender and extend shelf life.

items.title: Reduced trans‑fat content
items.content: Modern processing can produce oils with minimal trans‑fat, which is better for cardiovascular health.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: As with all fats, oils are calorie‑dense, so intake should be moderated.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to soy, peanut or other oil sources.

items.title: Oxidation and rancidity
items.content: Improper storage can lead to oxidation, producing off‑flavors and potentially harmful compounds.

items.title: PAH formation
items.content: Overheating certain oils can generate polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, which are considered possible carcinogens.

items.title: Environmental concerns
items.content: Production of some oils (e.g., palm oil) is linked to deforestation and loss of biodiversity.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Industrial oils are added to sauces, marinades, baked goods, confectionery and ready‑made mixes. They can be used for frying, baking or as a base for diet‑friendly formulations. When cooking with oil, follow recommended temperature limits to avoid overheating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store oil in a tightly sealed container in a cool, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep it refrigerated. Protect it from air and light to prevent oxidation. Discard oil that develops a rancid smell.

content.title: About
content.content: Tomato Juice, 100%, Low Sodium is a completely natural juice made from ripe tomatoes without added sugar or preservatives. It has a bright tomato flavor, moderate acidity, and minimal sodium, making it suitable for low‑salt diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes are a rich source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant linked to reduced risk of certain cancers.
Tomato juice is commonly used as a base for sauces, soups, and cocktails.
Low sodium is achieved by selecting tomatoes with naturally low salt content and using a special processing method.
It can be a healthy alternative to sugary soft drinks thanks to its refreshing taste without added sugar.
In many countries tomato juice is considered a comforting beverage during colder months.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene provides antioxidant protection, supports heart health, and may lower the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Ideal for individuals monitoring salt intake, including those with hypertension.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B6, niacin, and folate, which are important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal blood pressure.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Mostly water, it contributes to overall hydration.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, ranging from skin rashes to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The natural acidity may irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcer disease.

items.title: Natural sugars
items.content: Although no sugar is added, tomatoes contain natural sugars that may affect strict low‑glycemic diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled as a refreshing beverage, add it to smoothies, cocktails, or use it as a base for soups, sauces, and marinades. A pinch of fresh herbs or spices can enhance the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: After opening, keep the juice refrigerated in a tightly sealed container and consume within 5‑7 days. Unopened packages should be stored in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight.
